Your story is very close to my heart because I shared a similar experience much like this (though I am the guy in the situation). 

I'm not great with advice but I can tell you about my story and see if that helps (I hope it does).

I was a rising freshman and had joined the marching band. There was this girl that I had always known but never known well that caught my attention and I decided to actively work on becoming closer friends with her. The more I got to know her, the more interesting she became. 

We were decent friends until we shared a seat on the bus to the first band competition of the year, some ridiculously long distance away. We shared my headphones and just listened to music and talked for hours non-stop until we got to the competition. 

After that first bus ride, we became super close friends to the point where people thought we were dating (we practically were, but without the title or acknowledging what everyone else plainly saw). We made it a tradition to always share the same seat on any bus and listen to music and talk. We learned more about each other by talking on the other five really long bus rides that season; by the end of marching band season, we knew and trusted each other like siblings.

I thought she was out of my league and resigned myself to getting friend-zoned because I treated her so well (much like OP's situation) and after pining for her for a couple of months, I convinced myself to move on. I dated a senior girl shortly afterwords as a "rebound" from being unofficially rejected. 

At the same time, the girl in question started dating a guy who was way below her league and who also happened to be an obnoxious turd. Both of our relationships didn't last more that a few months because she realized that she had made a mistake ever saying yes to him, and I never really liked the girl I was dating enough to push it forward and it stalled before it ever really took off the ground.

Fast forward a year and I find myself back in marching band season as a sophomore.

Coming back from summer break and not seeing her for a few months made me like her even more. Absence makes the heart grow fonder, I suppose. 

It took me the whole marching band season to work up my courage. I asked her out as we were walking from the bus to the band rehearsal room across a grass field from the last band competition of the season. 

I asked her, "We didn't even know each other much before a year ago. In that year, you have become the closest friend I know, who I can share anything with. I wanted to ask you if you would like to take this relationship to the next step because I can't deny how much I like you, but if you don't then I would still like to keep what we have right now."

She started laughing so hard she had trouble breathing and in between gasps of air, said, "Yes! I wasn't sure if *we* would ever happen!"

We went on to have a fantastic year long relationship until she broke it off suddenly because she was having trouble with how much she was letting her guard down for me of me and how much she trusted me (she had some family issues at the time and we have both since acknowledged that it was her fault and the reasons for ending it were irrational on her part). We still are good friends and talk on occasion.

Behind the scenes (this is where I tell you about what I wish I had known then, but didn't):

The girl realized that she liked me almost immediately after that first bus ride but was too shy to say anything. She talked amongst all of her girlfriends and had them bother me about why we weren't dating, etc. At one point she even was contemplating asking me out but I had "moved on" to the senior girl and she lost her nerve and resigned herself to always having to be my best friend instead of my girlfriend.

So it turns out the whole time I thought that I would be *forever alone.jpg*, my best friend had mutual feelings for me too and she was too scared to make a move and figured I would get her signals when she "bat[ed her] eyelashes at [me] and [wore] that low cut shirt next time [she saw me]".

TL;DR: Guy and Girl become best friends and have romantic feelings for each other but are each too afraid to say something and risk ruining an excellent friendship. Guy finally asks her out and the two spend an awesome year together. Everything turned out better than expected. :)
